inputs.note: This is node_embedding_epoch_repr (the reproducible_flag=True kernel that clustering.py's node_embedding(..., reproducible_flag=True) actually calls -- NOT the plain node_embedding_epoch, which is only used when reproducible_flag=False). epoch_of_next_sample and epoch_of_next_negative_sample are deliberately recorded as all-zero (NOT the natural epoch-0 values, which are >=1 and would mean almost nothing fires) so every edge's positive update AND negative-sampling loop fire on this single call -- this isolates the per-edge SGD math from the outer epoch-loop scheduling. rng_state here is a single scalar (uint32), NOT a tau_rand advancing 3-int64 state -- negative sample target index is `node_order[(raw_index * (n + p + 1) * rng_state) % n_vertices]`, pure integer arithmetic, no RNG state mutation. updates[] accumulates positive+negative gradient contributions per from_node across the WHOLE block before being added into embedding at the end of the block (node_embedding itself then scales updates by (1-alpha)^2*0.5 AFTER this call and carries it to the next epoch -- that carry-over is NOT part of this kernel and is out of scope for this fixture). Expected embedding_after already has updates applied (this kernel applies them internally, in its last per-block loop) -- do NOT separately add updates_after to embedding_before.
